name: New York
tagline: Lake Erie to Orient Point, through Adirondack lakes, Finger Lakes vineyards and Catskill cloves.
intro: New York's byways run along the Great Lakes and the St. Lawrence, cross the Adirondacks on a string of named trails, circle the Finger Lakes and wind through the Catskills, the Hudson Valley and out to Long Island's North Fork. This chapter follows the New York State Scenic Byways Program of the New York State Department of Transportation, which lists 30 byways, four of them national. Several are parkways, such as the Taconic and the Bronx River, and the state law also counts its DEC Scenic Roads and state parkways as scenic byways, though those short segments are not listed here.

programs.label: New York State Scenic Byways Program
programs.issuer: New York State Department of Transportation

members.name: Lakes to Locks Passage, All American Road
members.blurb: From Waterford north to Rouses Point, the passage follows the Champlain Canal and then the western shores of Lake George and Lake Champlain, past the old forts at Ticonderoga and Crown Point.

members.name: Mohawk Towpath Byway, National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Twenty-six miles beside the Mohawk River and the old Erie Canal, from Waterford to the Stockade District of Schenectady, past canal locks and bridges and streets of houses built as early as the 1670s.

members.name: Great Lakes Seaway Trail, National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Seaway Trail runs 454 miles through New York from Ripley on Lake Erie, past Niagara Falls and along Lake Ontario, to the Thousand Islands and the St. Lawrence River at Massena, with lighthouses and harbors along the shore.

members.name: Palisades Scenic Byway, National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The New York stretch of the Palisades Interstate Parkway runs 26 miles through Rockland and Orange counties under stone-arched bridges and between forested buffers, ending at a traffic circle by the Bear Mountain Bridge.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Adirondack Trail
members.blurb: Route 30 crosses the whole Adirondack Park for 188 miles, from Fonda on the Mohawk north to Malone, past Indian, Long and Tupper lakes and the museum at Blue Mountain Lake.

members.name: Black River Trail
members.blurb: Ninety-four miles down the Black River valley from Rome to Dexter and the river's mouth at Black River Bay on Lake Ontario, with the Tug Hill Plateau on one side and the Adirondacks on the other.

members.name: Blue Ridge Road
members.blurb: Seventeen miles of county road through the woods between North Hudson and Newcomb along the southern edge of the High Peaks, past trailheads for the Dix Mountain and Hoffman Notch wildernesses and, oddly, a few buffalo.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Bronx River Parkway
members.blurb: Begun in 1907, the parkway follows the Bronx River for 13 miles through Westchester's first park, from the Bronx line to the plaza below Kensico Dam, on one of the first roads built for motorcars.

members.name: Catskill Mountains Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Route 28 runs 52 miles through the Central Catskills from Olive to Andes, past reservoirs of the New York City water supply and through Phoenicia, Pine Hill, Fleischmanns and Margaretville.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Cayuga Lake Scenic Byway
members.blurb: An 87-mile loop around Cayuga Lake past vineyards, lakeside bluffs and cattail marshes to the sites of the women's rights movement, with tiny Frontenac Island lying offshore at Union Springs.

members.name: Central Adirondack Trail
members.blurb: An arc through the middle of the Adirondacks from Glens Falls to Rome, by way of Lake George, Blue Mountain Lake and the Fulton Chain of Lakes at Old Forge, ending at the restored Fort Stanwix.

members.name: Dude Ranch Trail
members.blurb: A 40-mile loop out of Lake George village through Warrensburg, Stony Creek and Lake Luzerne, horse-ranch country in the southeastern Adirondacks, where rafting trips set out on the Sacandaga River.

members.name: Durham Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A web of country roads in the Town of Durham, 21 miles in all, below the northern escarpment of the Catskills, with stone bridges and walls, old farms and the Five State View across the Hudson Valley.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: High Peaks Byway (Route 73)
members.blurb: Route 73 climbs from the Northway at Exit 30 to Lake Placid, passing Chapel Pond, Roaring Brook Falls and the Cascade Lakes in the narrow passes below the Adirondacks' highest peaks.
members.note: Shown on the map as High Peaks Scenic Byway (NYS Route 73).

members.name: Historic Parkways of Long Island
members.blurb: Six Long Island parkways, among them the Wantagh, whose first stretch opened in 1929 as the causeway to Jones Beach, and the Ocean Parkway, which runs the length of Jones Beach Island to Captree.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Maple Traditions
members.blurb: Eighty miles from Lowville to Ogdensburg and the bridge to Canada, past sugarhouses boiling sap over wood fires, Amish fields and the American Maple Museum in Croghan.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Military Trail
members.blurb: Eighty-four miles from Rouses Point to Massena, on a road long used to move troops between Lake Champlain and the St. Lawrence, past the High Falls at Chateaugay and the Almanzo Wilder farm near Malone.

members.name: Mountain Cloves
members.blurb: Forty-one miles of roads around Hunter in the northern Catskills, through Stony Clove Notch on a route first cut for a tannery in the 1840s, in mountains that drew the Hudson River School painters.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: North Fork Trail
members.blurb: A 36-mile loop on Long Island's North Fork from Southold out to Orient Point, where Route 25 ends at the ferry landing, past wineries, broad farms and wetlands with glimpses of the water.

members.name: Olympic Trail
members.blurb: From Lake Ontario at Sackets Harbor to Keeseville near Lake Champlain, 170 miles across the northern Adirondacks by Cranberry, Tupper and Saranac lakes to Lake Placid, twice host of the Winter Olympics.

members.name: Revolutionary Byway
members.blurb: From Port Ontario on Lake Ontario to Albany, 158 miles that mostly follow the Mohawk River through Rome, Utica and Schenectady, past Fort Stanwix, the Oriskany Battlefield and other Revolutionary War sites.

members.name: Roosevelt-Marcy Trail
members.blurb: Route 28N follows Theodore Roosevelt's 1901 ride from Mount Marcy to the North Creek station, where he learned he would be president, through Newcomb and Minerva below the fire tower on Goodnow Mountain.

members.name: Route 20 Scenic Byway
members.blurb: U.S. 20 crosses the hills of Central New York for 108 miles from Duanesburg to LaFayette, on the line of the old Cherry Valley Turnpike, once lined with taverns for wagon traffic, now with farms and village main streets.

members.name: Scenic Route 90
members.blurb: Route 90 runs from Homer through Finger Lakes farm country and along the shore towns of Cayuga Lake to Montezuma, with a turn for Harriet Tubman's last home along the way.

members.name: Seneca Lake Byway
members.blurb: Nineteen miles of Route 414 along the southeast shore of Seneca Lake, from Clute Park in Watkins Glen to the state marine park at Lodi Point, above water more than 600 feet deep that never freezes.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Shawangunk Mountains
members.blurb: An 88-mile ring around the northern Shawangunk Ridge, said SHON-gum, through the Rondout and Wallkill valleys and the towns of New Paltz and Ellenville, with Mohonk Preserve and Minnewaska up on the ridge.

members.name: Southern Adirondack Trail
members.blurb: From Herkimer and the canal locks at Little Falls north to Speculator, 112 miles that loop around Piseco Lake, with a stop to dig crystals at the Herkimer Diamond Mine.

members.name: Taconic Parkway
members.blurb: The Taconic State Parkway winds 104 miles from Kensico Dam to Chatham, laid out by Gilmore Clarke for views of the Hudson Highlands and the Catskills, and listed whole on the National Register in 2005.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Upper Delaware (Route 97)
members.blurb: Route 97 follows the Delaware River from Port Jervis to Hancock, taking the tight bends of the Hawk's Nest and passing the Roebling Bridge, on a highway not finished until 1939.

members.name: WNY Southtowns Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A loop through the hills southeast of Buffalo on US 219 and Routes 240 and 242, from Orchard Park and the Roycroft Campus in East Aurora down to Ellicottville, past the steel figures of Griffis Sculpture Park.
members.note: Shown on the map as Western New York Southtowns Scenic Byway.
